Epilepsy clinic letter
Consultation: 15 January 2025
Patient: Alex Morgan, aged 36

Dear colleague,

Alex has an established diagnosis of epilepsy, currently of uncertain type. We discussed three event types today: nocturnal convulsions, daytime staring spells and brief morning jerks. Alex and their partner report no other event types.

The last nocturnal convulsion was on 12 August 2024, with none since. Daytime staring spells began in November 2024 and continue two to three times a week; I currently regard these as focal impaired-awareness seizures. The latest staring spell was on 13 January. Brief jerks of both arms after waking began in December 2024 and have occurred roughly every two weeks, most recently on 10 January. I regard the morning jerks as epileptic, although their precise classification remains uncertain. The staring spells and morning jerks have both been recurring during December and January. The absence of further nocturnal convulsions does not mean Alex is free of all seizures.

Alex reports continuing levetiracetam. We discussed adding lamotrigine, but agreed to defer starting it until the next review. This is a treatment proposal, not confirmation that Alex has taken it.

I requested a routine EEG today. It has not yet been performed and no result is available. This is the only EEG requested for Alex since 20 July 2024.

We will review the event descriptions and investigation findings at follow-up.

Epilepsy clinic letter
Consultation: 20 June 2025
Patient: Alex Morgan

Dear colleague,

Alex attended with their partner. Their established epilepsy diagnosis remains, with the precise epilepsy type still uncertain. The same three event types remain the complete reported history; neither describes an additional type.

The daytime staring spells are the events I called focal impaired-awareness seizures in January. They continued intermittently, most recently on 10 June. After reviewing the home videos and the detailed history today, I now diagnose these as functional non-epileptic spells. This reinterpretation applies to the same staring spells from their onset in November, including those described in the January letter. This is our first reclassification of any of Alex's events from epileptic to non-epileptic, and the decision was made today, 20 June 2025.

The morning jerks described in January remain epileptic in my assessment. They have continued roughly every two weeks, with the latest on 18 June. There have been no nocturnal convulsions since 12 August 2024. Reviewing the history up to today, the morning jerks have been the only active epileptic pattern since December; the staring spells are a separate non-epileptic pattern. I cannot establish a more precise seizure type from this review.

Alex confirms that they have never taken lamotrigine. The addition discussed in January was not enacted. They report continuing levetiracetam.

The routine EEG requested on 15 January was performed on 10 February. Its report became available to our clinical team on 12 February and described no epileptiform abnormalities. The change in interpretation above is my clinical assessment of the staring events, not an inference from a normal EEG alone. I requested a separate repeat EEG today to investigate the continuing morning jerks; it has not yet been performed.

We will meet again in July to discuss progress.
